explanation: Recursively decide whether to include each input element. Record the selected values once all input positions have been considered; inclusion and exclusion cover the full power set.
timeComplexity: O(n·2^n) for n>0: the 2^n subset leaves contain n·2^(n−1) total elements to construct/copy; empty input takes O(1).
spaceComplexity: O(n²) conservative working-space bound for copied partial lists retained along a depth-n path, plus O(n·2^n) output element storage.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/power_set.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: A subset corresponds uniquely to one include/exclude decision for every input value. Each recursion branch makes one such decision and leaves earlier decisions intact. Therefore all 2^n subsets, including the empty subset, are produced exactly once for distinct input values.
walkthrough: For [6,9], the four include/exclude paths produce [6,9], [6], [9], and []. Python explores exclusion first, while C++/Java explore inclusion first; the judge ignores subset and element order.
edgeCases: An empty set returns a list containing the empty subset.
The input is a set; distinct values avoid duplicate subset identities.
Copies keep previously generated subsets unchanged.
